scope: M4.2 immutable create_ticket proposal and human decision without provider write

omitted_axes.reason: M4.2 exposes HTTP/application and persistence contracts with no UI surface.

test_cases.requirement: Immutable canonical proposal with trusted caller and actor provenance
test_cases.risk: Client-controlled actors/digests or noncanonical parameters receive approval authority.
prerequisites: Fake CapabilityResolver and trusted actor context fixtures exist.
steps: Create one valid proposal; inspect normalized projection and durable read-back.
expected_results: Server derives provenance, exact bindings, digest, logical ID and expiry; no provider write occurs.
evidence_to_capture: Sanitized request/projection, fake resolver input/output and zero provider-call proof.

test_cases.requirement: Closed create schema and title/description bounds
test_cases.risk: Actor spoofing, digest overrides or ambiguous Unicode/whitespace change approved intent.
prerequisites: Proposal route and deterministic canonicalizer exist.
steps: Exercise absent/non-string/empty/over-limit/NUL/leading-trailing-space values, Unicode normalization and every forbidden extra field.
expected_results: Invalid inputs return 422 before persistence; canonical equivalents bind one server-computed digest; client actor/authority/digest/provider/logical-ID fields are rejected.
evidence_to_capture: Named validation matrix, digest recomputation and store/gateway zero-call assertions.

test_cases.risk: Cross-Workspace callers learn proposal existence or mutate another Workspace decision.
prerequisites: Two Workspace principals and one persisted proposal exist.
steps: Call create/read/approve/reject with missing auth, wrong path Workspace, unauthorized principal and authorized missing proposal.
expected_results: 401/403 occur before proposal lookup; authorized absence is 404; no decision/audit row appears on denied calls.
evidence_to_capture: Route/status matrix, store-call ordering and database row counts.

test_cases.requirement: Human-only decisions and policy-controlled separation of duties
test_cases.risk: Model/system actors approve or a blanket proposer/approver inequality changes policy.
prerequisites: Human/model/system actor contexts and SoD policy fixtures exist.
steps: Attempt approve/reject from model/system; approve as an authorized human under no-SoD policy; repeat same-actor approval under explicit SoD policy.
expected_results: Model/system decisions are forbidden; authorized human succeeds without blanket inequality; explicit SoD policy denies only the configured same-actor case.
evidence_to_capture: Decision matrix, authorizer reasons and durable decision/audit proof.

test_cases.requirement: Concurrent approve/reject has one atomic winner
test_cases.risk: Two decisions commit or clients assume actor-specific precedence.
prerequisites: Clean proposed revision and two concurrent database sessions exist.
steps: Release concurrent approve and reject attempts against the same expected revision; repeat enough times to cover either scheduler winner.
expected_results: Exactly one CAS commits; loser returns persisted AlreadyDecided decision/revision; one decision row and ordered audit event exist without assumed precedence.
evidence_to_capture: Concurrent outcomes, revision, decision row count and audit sequence.

test_cases.requirement: PostgreSQL material immutability and append-only audit reconstruction
test_cases.risk: Approved target/parameters/provenance are edited or audit is incomplete/mutable.
prerequisites: Migrated clean database and one decided proposal exist.
steps: Reload the proposal, reconstruct provenance, attempt every material-column update and audit update/delete, then create a materially changed replacement proposal.
expected_results: Read-back matches canonical intent; mutations fail; audit is ordered/append-only; replacement has a new proposal/logical ID and requires a new decision.
evidence_to_capture: Projection/digest comparison, database rejection reasons and replacement identities.

test_cases.requirement: Stale, temporary authority and expiry projections remain distinct
test_cases.risk: Old approval silently executes under changed semantics or temporary revocation destroys approval.
prerequisites: Approved proposal and deterministic current resolver/policy clock fixtures exist.
steps: Temporarily deny execution authority; change capability/binding/policy digest independently; advance beyond proposal expiry; inspect lifecycle and executable projection.
expected_results: Temporary denial leaves approved/non-stale; each material mismatch is stale/non-executable; expiry blocks new execution; no case edits the immutable proposal or invokes provider write.
evidence_to_capture: Reason-code matrix, unchanged lifecycle/material digest and zero provider calls.

test_cases.requirement: No provider write, narrow resolver independence and no M1-M3 regression
test_cases.risk: M4.2 imports M4.1 concrete code, performs a side effect or breaks existing behavior.
prerequisites: Docker services and clean migrated database are available.
steps: Run focused M4.2 tests, full pytest, Ruff, Compose/Alembic checks and dependency/diff inspection.
expected_results: All checks pass; only CapabilityResolver protocol/fake is used; zero SupportToolGateway writes; existing behavior remains green.
evidence_to_capture: Command summaries, import/dependency inventory, provider call proof and clean status.
